summary.headline: Epigral Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR709 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 25% from 27% amid West Asia cost pressures.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 15% YoY to INR709 crore on higher volumes and realisations, while EBITDA rose 10% to INR179 crore and margin eased to 25% from 27%. Adjusted PAT grew 25% to INR99 crore against INR79 crore a year earlier, though the prior-year reported PAT of INR160 crore included an INR81 crore deferred tax credit. ROCE fell to 16% (18% excluding capital work in progress) and net debt/EBITDA rose to 0.8x. Management announced a Board-approved INR600 crore plan for an epoxy resin and formulations plant (125,000 tpa) and a multipurpose plant (MPP).

financial_highlights.value: INR35,000-36,000/t in Q1 FY27 (about INR31,000-32,000 currently)

segments.name: Chlor-alkali (caustic soda/ECU)
segments.commentary: Caustic soda capacity utilisation about 75% in Q1 FY27. ECU realisation about INR35,000-36,000 in Q1, easing to about INR31,000-32,000 currently; chlorine realisation about negative INR4,000.

segments.name: Epichlorohydrin (ECH)
segments.commentary: ECH utilisation about 70-75% in Q1. Current ECH realisation about INR180-185/t, down from INR200-210 during the war-time peak. Capacity expansion from 50,000 to 100,000 tpa is progressing on time and within budget, with commissioning expected in a couple of months.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: CPVC utilisation about 50-55% in Q1 as pipe customers managed PVC inventory amid volatility. Realisation about INR110-115/kg currently. Management expects demand to pick up from Q3 with monsoon seasonality; a 75,000 tpa expansion is underway.

segments.name: Chlorotoluenes / chloromethanes / peroxide
segments.commentary: Chloromethanes running about 100%; hydrogen peroxide about 85-90%. Chlorotoluenes capex of about INR250 crore done; expected revenue INR300-350 crore at optimum level, with the combined chlorotoluene and MPP top line targeted at INR700-800 crore.

guidance_outlook: Long-term growth target of 15-20% CAGR over 3-5 years in top line and bottom line, with an internal aspiration of about 20%.
Epoxy and MPP projects together: peak revenue of INR1,300-1,500 crore once plants reach optimum levels; ROCE target about 20%, with margins lower than the existing 22-24% range.
Capex of about INR400 crore each in FY27 and FY28; the INR600 crore epoxy and MPP project funded about 40% internally and 60% debt.
Pilot facility for epoxy and MPP expected to be operational by September 2026 (Q2 FY27); MPP completion targeted in FY28.
Chlorotoluene and MPP derivatives target of INR500 crore revenue within about three years, with ramp-up likely in FY29-FY30.
capex_capacity: Epoxy resin and formulations: 125,000 tpa, with more than 50% of raw material value sourced internally (ECH and caustic soda). Management said LER will be a smaller share of the mix.

Multipurpose plant (MPP) for chlorotoluene and ECH downstream derivatives (pharma/agrochemical intermediates, water treatment chemicals); the combined epoxy and MPP project is INR600 crore, with no split given.
ECH capacity doubling from 50,000 to 100,000 tpa; post-expansion, about 50% of ECH is to be consumed in-house and 50% sold.
CPVC expansion of 75,000 tpa underway, progressing on schedule and within budget.
Power: no further captive power plant; energy to come from long-term solar and wind hybrid contracts (two 20 MW contracts).
demand_pricing: Epoxy demand estimated at 2.5-3 lakh tonnes, expected to grow at double-digit rates; management expects export opportunities to Europe after an India-EU FTA.
Caustic: management expects India to remain a net importer given alumina capacity growth; short-term oversupply risk for a couple of years.

CPVC: management said near-term overcapacity is likely as Grasim and others add capacity; pricing of CPVC is about INR110-115/kg and ethylene-based PVC pricing is not expected to be materially affected by the recent MIP.
Glycerin/ECH: management said glycerin prices are driven by palm oil and biodiesel policy as well as crude and propylene, and that ECH prices are volatile.
Management said the 2.5-3 lakh tonne epoxy demand is growing at double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Is the epoxy capacity announcement mainly LER or does it include value-added products, and what is the market size split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 125,000 tpa capacity includes LER plus value-added and formulations, with LER a smaller share of the mix. Epoxy demand is estimated at 2.5-3 lakh tonnes, growing at double-digit rates, with Europe seen as an export opportunity after an India-EU FTA.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q1 FY27 and Q4 FY26 ECU realisations and utilisation levels?
qa_highlights.answer: ECU was about INR35,000-36,000/t in Q1 FY27 and about INR30,000 in Q4 FY26, easing to about INR31,000-32,000 currently. Utilisation was about 75% for caustic soda, 70-75% for ECH, 50-55% for CPVC, about 100% for chloromethanes and 85-90% for peroxide.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of the INR600 crore capex between epoxy and MPP, and peak revenue from both projects?
qa_highlights.answer: No split was given; the INR600 crore is a combined figure. Peak revenue from both projects together is expected at INR1,300-1,500 crore once plants reach optimum levels, with ROCE targeted around 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the epoxy margin dilution change the 22-24% combined margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said epoxy margins will be lower in percentage terms because turnover per unit of investment is about 3-4x that of the existing portfolio. Project evaluation focuses on ROCE, which epoxy still meets.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR600 crore project mean peak total revenue of INR4,000-4,500 crore, given current revenue of about INR2,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rejected that reading. It said existing capacity can still ramp up and the ECH and CPVC expansions are due in a couple of months, and that epoxy and MPP together add INR1,300-1,500 crore at peak.

qa_highlights.question: What growth rate should be expected and is the target on top line or bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15-20% CAGR over 3-5 years, with an internal aspiration of about 20%, for both top line and bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: How do the CPVC and PVC pricing respond to the recent MIP, and what is the outlook for CPVC demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MIP mainly hit carbide-based PVC, not the ethylene-based PVC Epigral uses, so no major impact is expected. CPVC realisation is about INR110-115/kg. Demand is expected to pick up from Q3 with monsoon seasonality, though near-term overcapacity is likely as new capacity comes on.

qa_highlights.question: What are the chlorotoluenes and MPP capex, revenue and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Chlorotoluenes capex of about INR250 crore is done, with expected revenue of INR300-350 crore at optimum. Including MPP, the combined top line is targeted at INR700-800 crore, at an estimated margin of about 22-23%, with 1.5-2 years to optimum utilisation.

risks_watch: Epoxy and MPP margins will be lower than the 22-24% range, with ROCE of about 20% the stated offset; the margin trajectory of the combined business is not guided numerically.
CPVC overcapacity as Grasim and others add capacity, with utilisation at 50-55% in Q1 FY27 and a demand recovery expected only from Q3.
Caustic oversupply risk for a couple of years from domestic capacity additions, with utilisation at about 75% and ECU easing from INR35,000-36,000 to INR31,000-32,000/t.
ECH realisation fell from INR200-210/kg at the war-time peak to about INR180-185/t currently; ECH and glycerin prices are volatile, linked to crude, propylene and biodiesel policy.
Execution: the pilot facility is due by September 2026, ECH capacity doubling to 100,000 tpa and the 75,000 tpa CPVC expansion are due in a couple of months, and the MPP is targeted for FY28.
Leverage and returns: net debt/EBITDA rose to 0.8x from 0.6x, ROCE fell to 16% from 24%, and the INR600 crore project is 60% debt-funded.
Capex of about INR400 crore each in FY27 and FY28 keeps balance-sheet strain and the ROCE trajectory in focus.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 FY27 presented a highly challenging operating environment across all the segments, including chemicals.
Even against this volatile backdrop Epigral demonstrated a resilience, delivering a revenue growth of 15% and EBITDA margin of 25%.
So definitely, EBITDA margin in terms of percentage, definitely, it is coming lower.
Rather than giving guidance on margin, I can tell you that ROCE, we are targeting in the range of 20%.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term growth, expansion execution and the epoxy and MPP projects, but cautious and at times evasive on near-term pricing and margins. It declined to give a breakup of the INR600 crore capex or a numeric margin guide for the new projects, and said near-term PVC, ECH and caustic prices are too volatile to forecast.
